key_insight: A local two-stage LLM pipeline can accurately identify hepatocellular carcinoma reports and extract structured pathology variables from German free-text reports without sending patient data outside the institution.
clinical_relevance: This could speed up pathology quality control and registry curation by turning unstructured reports into usable structured data in a privacy-preserving way.
method: Stage 1 used a lightweight gatekeeper model to screen 2,864 reports for confirmed HCC cases.
Stage 2 used a higher-capacity open-weight model to extract 15 predefined histopathology variables into JSON.
Both stages were compared against expert-curated reference annotations using accuracy, macro F1, and Cohen’s kappa.
evidence_signal: The best gatekeeper achieved zero classification errors, and the top Stage 2 model reached near-perfect agreement with the reference standard, with Macro F1 > 0.99.
watch_item: Performance was shown on a specific German HCC report setting, so external validation is needed before broader deployment.
paper_title: Large Language Models for Structured Information Extraction from German Histopathology Reports - Hepatocellular Carcinoma
